name: Longer Ray7S 40W
tagline: The cutting Ray7S: a 40W diode with air pump in a Class 1 cabinet, for thick wood and dark acrylic
tldr: The Ray7S 40W is the top of Longer's new enclosed range: $849.99 for the Basic Set on Longer's store in October 2026, the only Ray7S version with the air pump in the box. Longer shows it cutting 30 mm basswood and 35 mm black acrylic, without stating the number of passes; by our estimate it cuts 10–15 mm basswood in one pass. Klipper firmware, 600 mm/s and a Class 1 cabinet come with a modest 305 × 300 mm bed, and it costs about $850 less than xTool's enclosed 40W.
mainObjective: Cutting thick plywood and dark acrylic in a closed Class 1 cabinet at home

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W version of the Longer Ray7S. Pick it if cutting thick plywood, boxes or dark acrylic is the main job and you want the beam contained in a Class 1 cabinet. Compare the other Ray7S versions with the chips above if you mostly engrave: smaller modules have finer spots and cost far less. Plan an outdoor exhaust route from day one.
proTips: Duct the exhaust outside: at 40W a closed cabinet fills with smoke fast. Split thick cuts into several faster passes to limit charring and flare-ups, and keep the tinted lid clean. Lower the power well under half for photos to keep the wide spot from blurring detail.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 40W Ray7S brings real cutting power into a Class 1 cabinet for well under $1,000, with the air pump included, Klipper firmware and 600 mm/s motion. Few enclosed 40W diodes cost this little.
editorialDepth.limitations: The 305 × 300 mm bed is small for signs and panels, the wide spot is a compromise for fine engraving, and Longer's 30 mm / 35 mm cut claims come without a pass count. It is a brand-new machine: exhaust capacity and cabinet durability have not been independently tested.

faq.question: Can the Ray7S 40W really cut 30 mm basswood?
faq.answer: Longer's product page shows 30 mm basswood and 35 mm black acrylic cuts, without saying how many passes they take; such depths always need several passes on a diode. By our estimate, the 40W cuts 10–15 mm basswood in one pass with its included air pump.

faq.question: Ray7S 40W or xTool S1 40W?
faq.answer: The Ray7S 40W costs $849.99 against about $1,699 for the xTool S1 40W (October 2026). The S1 offers a 498 × 319 mm bed, a mature ecosystem and an IR option; the Ray7S halves the price with a smaller bed and no track record yet.

faq.question: Ray7S 40W or open Ray7 40W?
faq.answer: The open Ray7 40W costs $669.99 and has a larger 405 × 400 mm bed, but no air pump in the box and no cabinet. The Ray7S 40W adds $180 for the Class 1 enclosure, Klipper firmware and the included pump.
